brand.label: Camera Brand
brand.tooltip: Select your camera manufacturer. This will auto-configure connection settings.
brand.help_text: Choose the brand of your camera. If you don't see your brand listed, select 'Generic ONVIF' if your camera supports ONVIF, or 'Generic RTSP' for manual configuration.

model.label: Camera Model
model.tooltip: Optional: Select specific model for optimized settings
model.help_text: Selecting a specific model will pre-configure the best settings for your camera. If your exact model isn't listed, you can skip this and the system will use generic settings for your brand.

name.label: Camera Name
name.tooltip: Give your camera a descriptive name
name.help_text: Choose a name that helps you identify this camera's location or purpose.

host.label: IP Address
host.tooltip: Enter the camera's IP address on your local network
host.help_text: This is the local network IP address assigned to your camera. You can find this in your camera's app, web interface, or your router's DHCP client list.
host.troubleshooting: If you can't find the IP address, check your camera's mobile app settings, use the manufacturer's discovery tool, or check your router's connected devices list.

port.label: RTSP Port
port.help_text: The RTSP port is used for video streaming. Most cameras use port 554, but some brands like Foscam use port 88. This is automatically set based on your camera brand.

username.label: Username
username.help_text: Enter the username you use to log into your camera's web interface or app. Common defaults are 'admin' but you should have changed this during setup.
username.security_note: For Tapo cameras, you need to create a separate 'Camera Account' in the Tapo app under Advanced Settings before using RTSP.

password.label: Password
password.help_text: Enter the password for your camera. This will be encrypted before storing. Never use default passwords like '12345' or 'admin'.
password.security_note: Passwords are encrypted using military-grade encryption before storage. Special characters may need to be avoided in some camera models.
password.troubleshooting: If connection fails with correct credentials, try removing special characters like !@#$%^&* from your password.

protocol.label: Protocol
protocol.help_text: The communication protocol used to receive video from the camera.

options.label: RTSP
options.description: Real-Time Streaming Protocol - Most common and recommended for all cameras

options.label: ONVIF
options.description: Auto-discover stream URLs using ONVIF standard - Good for generic cameras

options.label: MJPEG
options.description: Motion JPEG over HTTP - Fallback option, higher bandwidth usage

protocol.recommendation: Use RTSP for best performance. Use ONVIF if you're unsure of stream URLs. MJPEG is a fallback for older cameras.

transport.label: Transport
transport.help_text: TCP is more reliable and recommended for most scenarios. UDP may offer lower latency but can lose packets.

options.label: UDP
options.description: Lower latency, may lose packets - Use only if needed

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.help_text: Higher resolutions provide better image quality but require more bandwidth and processing power. For live viewing on Raspberry Pi, 1080p or 720p is recommended.
resolution.recommendation: Use 1080p or 720p for live viewing, 4K for recording if your camera supports it.

frame_rate.label: Frame Rate
frame_rate.help_text: Higher frame rates produce smoother video but require more bandwidth. 15-20 FPS is sufficient for most security applications.
frame_rate.recommendation: 15 FPS for most cameras, 20-30 FPS for PTZ or high-motion areas

stream_path.label: Stream Path
stream_path.tooltip: URL path to camera's video stream
stream_path.help_text: The URL path component for accessing the camera's video stream. This is automatically configured based on your camera brand and model.
stream_path.manual_override: Only change this if auto-configuration fails and you know the correct path from your camera's documentation.

associated_game.label: Associated Game
associated_game.tooltip: Link this camera to an escape room game
associated_game.help_text: Associate this camera with a specific escape room game to enable game-triggered recording, event correlation, and game-specific viewing modes.

ptz.label: PTZ Control
ptz.help_text: If your camera supports PTZ (Pan-Tilt-Zoom), you can control camera movement remotely. This includes preset positions, auto-patrol routes, and manual control.
ptz.requirements: Requires ONVIF support or brand-specific API. Enable PTZ in camera settings first.

audio.label: Audio
audio.help_text: Enables audio streaming from the camera's built-in microphone. Useful for announcements or ambient sound monitoring.
audio.note: Not all cameras support audio. Check your camera specifications.

two_way_audio.label: Two-Way Audio
two_way_audio.help_text: Allows you to speak through the camera's built-in speaker. Requires camera with speaker and supported codec.
two_way_audio.requirements: Camera must have speaker, ONVIF Profile T, or brand-specific API support
two_way_audio.note: Tapo cameras support two-way audio via app only, not via ONVIF/RTSP

ir_control.label: IR / Night Vision
ir_control.help_text: Control the camera's infrared LEDs for night vision.

modes.auto: Camera automatically switches between day and night mode based on light sensor
modes.on: IR LEDs always on - forces night vision mode (black and white)
modes.off: IR LEDs always off - color mode only

ir_control.recommendation: Use 'Auto' mode for automatic switching based on ambient light

dual_stream.label: Dual Stream
dual_stream.help_text: Modern cameras support multiple simultaneous video streams with different resolutions and quality settings.

streams.sub: Low resolution for live viewing and mobile (480p-720p, 10-15 FPS)

dual_stream.benefit: Reduces bandwidth and processing load while maintaining high-quality recordings

onvif.label: ONVIF Support
onvif.help_text: ONVIF is an open standard for IP cameras that enables automatic discovery, stream detection, PTZ control, and events.

profiles.S: Basic streaming and PTZ - Most common
profiles.T: Advanced features including H.265 and two-way audio

onvif.note: Tapo cameras support Profile S only

connection_failed.title: Connection Failed
common_causes: Camera is not on the same network as EscapePlan
RTSP port is blocked by firewall
Camera RTSP is disabled in settings

solutions.action: Check if RTSP port is open
solutions.command: Use Test Connection button or VLC player

solutions.expected: Can log into camera web interface with same username/password

solutions.location: Camera settings > Network > RTSP (varies by brand)

authentication_failed.title: Authentication Failed
common_causes: Special characters in password not properly encoded
Tapo camera - no Camera Account created
solutions: Verify credentials by logging into camera web interface
For Tapo: Create Camera Account in app (Advanced Settings > Camera Account)
Try removing special characters from password
For Foscam: Create user via desktop app, not web interface

stream_timeout.title: Stream Timeout / Buffering
common_causes: Camera overloaded with too many connections
solutions: Reduce number of simultaneous viewers
Use sub-stream for live viewing instead of main stream
Switch camera to wired ethernet if on WiFi
Increase timeout setting to 20-30 seconds
Update camera firmware to latest version

no_video_stream.title: No Video Stream Found
common_causes: Wrong stream path for camera model
solutions: Use ONVIF auto-discovery to find correct stream URL
Test stream URL in VLC player first
Check camera documentation for exact stream path
Try both /Streaming/ and /streaming/ (case sensitive)
Enable H.264 in camera settings (some only support H.265)

ptz_not_working.title: PTZ Controls Not Responding
common_causes: PTZ not enabled in camera view area settings
solutions: Enable ONVIF in camera settings
Create view area with PTZ enabled (Axis cameras)
Create separate ONVIF user account
For Axis: Try VAPIX commands instead of ONVIF
Verify camera actually has PTZ hardware (not digital PTZ)

poor_image_quality.title: Poor Image Quality / Low FPS
common_causes: Using main stream for live view
solutions: Use sub-stream for live viewing
Limit to 3-4 cameras viewing simultaneously
Reduce resolution or frame rate
Use wired ethernet instead of WiFi
Enable H.264+ / H.265+ smart compression in camera

steps.title: Select Camera Brand
steps.description: Choose your camera manufacturer from the dropdown
steps.tip: If unsure, check the camera label or packaging

steps.title: Select Model (Optional)
steps.description: Pick your specific model for optimized settings
steps.tip: Can skip this if model not listed - generic brand settings will be used

steps.title: Enter Connection Details
steps.description: Provide camera name, IP address, username, and password
steps.tip: Find IP address in camera app or router settings

steps.title: Test Connection
steps.tip: This validates network connectivity and stream access

steps.title: Configure Features
steps.description: Enable PTZ, audio, or other features if supported
steps.tip: Features are auto-detected based on camera model

steps.title: Associate with Game
steps.description: Link camera to an escape room game (optional)
steps.tip: Enables game-triggered recording and event correlation

steps.title: Save Camera
steps.tip: You can edit settings anytime from the camera list

network: Use wired ethernet instead of WiFi for stable connections
Place cameras on dedicated VLAN (10.10.10.0/24) isolated from internet
Assign static IP addresses to cameras in router DHCP reservation
Use Gigabit switches for 4K camera installations
security: Create unique passwords for each camera
Never expose cameras directly to the internet
performance: Use sub-stream for live viewing to reduce load
Limit main stream to 1080p or 2K on Raspberry Pi
reliability: Use UPS backup power for cameras and network equipment
Set up automatic camera restart on connection failure
Keep camera firmware up to date

glossary.rtsp: Real-Time Streaming Protocol - The standard for streaming video over IP networks
glossary.onvif: Open Network Video Interface Forum - An open standard ensuring camera interoperability
glossary.ptz: Pan-Tilt-Zoom - Camera movement controls (left/right, up/down, zoom in/out)
glossary.fps: Frames Per Second - Number of images displayed per second (higher = smoother video)
glossary.codec: Compression format for video (H.264, H.265/HEVC, MJPEG)
glossary.bitrate: Data rate of video stream in kilobits per second (higher = better quality, more bandwidth)
glossary.gop: Group of Pictures - Keyframe interval (distance between full frames)
glossary.sub_stream: Lower-resolution stream for live viewing and mobile
glossary.tcp: Transmission Control Protocol - Reliable network transport
glossary.udp: User Datagram Protocol - Fast but unreliable network transport
glossary.h264: Common video compression codec, widely supported
glossary.h265: Advanced codec with better compression (half the bitrate of H.264)
glossary.aac: Advanced Audio Coding - High-quality audio format
glossary.g711: Audio codec for telephony, used in two-way audio
glossary.ir: Infrared - Invisible light used for night vision
glossary.poe: Power over Ethernet - Provides both network and power via single cable
glossary.dhcp: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol - Automatic IP assignment
glossary.static_ip: Fixed IP address that doesn't change

bandwidth.title: Bandwidth Warning
bandwidth.message: Multiple 4K cameras may exceed Raspberry Pi network capacity
bandwidth.recommendation: Use 1080p or 2K for most cameras, reserve 4K for critical angles

wifi.title: WiFi Reliability Warning
wifi.message: WiFi cameras may experience connection drops
wifi.recommendation: Use wired ethernet for cameras when possible, especially for PTZ

security.title: Security Warning
security.recommendation: Change all camera passwords immediately. Never use 'admin' or '12345'

transcoding.title: Performance Warning
transcoding.message: Transcoding multiple streams may overload Raspberry Pi
transcoding.recommendation: Use camera's native H.264 streams when possible, limit simultaneous transcodes to 2-3
